means: No colour information at all - one hue worth of values, in practice black and white.
does: Greyscales the ENTIRE frame, and it is among the strongest tags in this whole vocabulary. studio/cards/shot_fx_screentone.json measured exactly this: a clause meant to lay a subtle tonal veil over a thinking face ('tonal overlay, monochrome shading, screentone wash') came back fully greyscale, and the review states plainly that monochrome is a very strong danbooru tag and will greyscale the entire frame. Pure danbooru grammar - a binary attribute, not a mood - so it silently overrides every colour tag in the prompt.
reach_for_it: flashbacks, manga inserts, a noir beat - when you want the colour GONE, all of it. If what you actually want is DESATURATED rather than absent, do it in the grade instead: studio/looks/noir.json uses hue=s=0 and measured SATAVG at exactly 0.000, deterministically and for free, with no token spent and no risk of it half-landing.
used_in: studio/looks/noir.json tags ('monochrome, greyscale, high contrast, dramatic shadow, film noir'), and anime.color.setting/monochrome_memory
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
